extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, policymakers, researchers, trademark analysts, and IP office staff who use or interpret WIPO trademark statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and definitions for interpreting WIPO trademark dataset figures (resident vs non-resident filings, class counts, absolute vs equivalent counts, Nice classification mapping, coverage and comparability caveats). Targeted at users analysing trademark filing and registration statistics across offices, origins and sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident filing decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: This figure shows the total growth or decrease in application class counts for each office, broken down by the respective contributions of resident and non-resident applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing growth or decline in application class counts, split the total change into contributions from resident filings and non-resident filings to understand drivers of change. Figures and charts in the publication present this decomposition for offices and selected country groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin determination (resident = origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of a trademark application is determined by the residence of the applicant. An application filed at a regional office is considered a resident filing if the applicant is a resident of one of the relevant member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the applicant's residence as the origin for 'by origin' statistics. For applications filed at regional offices, classify them as resident if the applicant resides in a member state of that regional office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute count vs equivalent count (filing activity abroad)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark application filing activity by origin includes the number of classes specified in resident applications and in applications filed abroad and is based on an absolute not equivalent count. This figure distinguishes between absolute and equivalent counts for filing activity abroad; that is, resident applications are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand whether a chart/table uses absolute counts (simple sum of classes specified) or equivalent counts (adjusted measure) when comparing filing activity abroad. The publication sometimes shows the equivalent/absolute count ratio to indicate differences between these measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application class count = number of classes specified
rubrics_metrics.description: The office and origin data shown consist of absolute rather than equivalent application class counts. The origin and office data shown consist of absolute rather than equivalent application class counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the tables, remember counts reflect the number of Nice classes specified (absolute class counts). Comparisons should account for this (e.g., multi-class vs single-class filing systems are not adjusted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations data not adjusted for single-class vs multi-class systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Data are based on the numbers of registrations recorded; that is, differences between single-class and multi-class registration systems across IP offices are not taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious comparing registration totals across offices with different registration systems—raw registration counts may be influenced by whether an office uses single-class or multi-class registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of goods vs services in Nice Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 45-class Nice Classification, the first 34 classes indicate goods and the remaining 11 refer to services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this split when aggregating or comparing 'goods' vs 'services' class shares. For complete class descriptions refer to the Nice Classification at www.wipo.int/classifications/nice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry sector mapping (Edital definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry sectors based on class groups are those defined by Edital. Some industry sectors are abbreviated. See annex B for full definitions and the composition of Nice goods and services classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing sectoral shares (e.g., 'Research and technology', 'Health', 'Clothing and accessories'), use the Edital grouping provided in the annex for consistent class-to-sector mapping; beware abbreviated sector labels in figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of 'registrations in force' percentages by registration year
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated as follows: the number of trademark registrations issued in year t and in force in 2022 divided by the total number of trademark registrations issued in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this explicit formula when reproducing or interpreting the 'registrations in force by registration year' series to ensure consistency with the publication's methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and coverage notes (number of reporting offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Totals by geographical region are WIPO estimates based on data covering 168 offices. Figures based on non-resident filing data from 137 IP offices. World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 152 IP offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that different figures/tables use different numbers of reporting offices; check the source note for the coverage appropriate to each table/figure before generalising results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability caveat due to procedural differences across offices
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO collects data from IP offices using a common questionnaire and methodology. However, because of differences in the application processing procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized. Therefore, caution should be exercised when making comparisons across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-interpreting small differences across offices; where possible, complement WIPO aggregates with office-level methodological notes or perform harmonisation adjustments before cross-office comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations in force reflect maintained trademark rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark rights can be maintained indefinitely by paying renewal fees at defined intervals. Trademarks in force provides information on the volume of trademark registrations currently active, as well as the historical trademark life cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'registrations in force' as a measure of active trademark rights; analysis of renewal/age profiles can indicate life-cycle dynamics (e.g., longevity, renewal behaviour) rather than new filing activity alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-resident share (%) and growth rate (%) metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and tables report non-resident share (%) and growth rate (%) for offices, origins and sectors (e.g., 'Non-resident share (%)', 'Growth rate (%)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting these percentages, ensure denominators are understood (e.g., share of classes, growth over prior year) and confirm whether counts are absolute/equivalent as noted in the specific figure/table.
